# Ordered cargo itineraries

Plan mixed cargo and ordered market or company\-stock work through two to four towns\.

New v3 pooled runs offer Fleet &gt; Inspect / edit route, also reachable from a selected owned ship's deck or Harbor\. Choose an owned ship, then draft two to four unique town stops with one to eight ordered actions each, at most 24 total\. Add, remove or reorder cards and expand an action to edit its fields\. Drafting and inspecting pause playback without changing stocks, cash or time\.

Buy and Sell exchange the named good with the public market for its exact bulk price\. Load and Unload transfer owned stock between the actual docked ship and its company town stock without payment\. No owned facility means no town warehouse\. Different goods can remain aboard together within the combined hold capacity; unmentioned goods are never discarded\.

Every action executes once per visit, choosing the largest whole quantity between its minimum and maximum that current stock, capacity and real funds permit\. Maximum is an order cap, not a hold target\. A partial qualifying order advances once\. Below minimum, Skip continues with no transaction; Wait keeps that exact action and stops\. Earlier completed buys or transfers never repeat because another instruction waits\.

Buy limits include maximum marginal ask, company cash reserve and a per\-order spending cap; Sell uses a minimum marginal bid\. Price zero means unrestricted and a blank spending cap means unrestricted within actual funds\. Loading can preserve a fractional town\-stock reserve\. Maximum and minimum cargo quantities are whole units; coin and warehouse reserves support four decimal places\. Remote quotes describe current conditions, not reserved future prices or permission to move goods\.

Each ship can use eight itinerary operations per economic day, counting successful orders, intentional skips and departure\. Eight commands can leave departure for tomorrow\. Repeated Run dockside actions, pause and save/load cannot reset this budget\. Ships keep the ordinary priority and ID order, real voyages and shared company cash; a blocked ship does not prevent the other ships from acting\.

Apply draft assigns the route and leaves actions paused\. Replacing a route requires Manual control, an actual dock included in the new plan, no partially completed old stop and no itinerary operations already performed today\. Advance a day after completed work before replacing it\. Viewing never requires empty cargo; applying preserves it\. Equivalent reapplication keeps progress\. Manual travel elsewhere does not reset the next stop; return there before resuming\.

Draft Grain–Flour–Bread loop resolves the actual role towns: A unloads two Flour and two Logs and loads up to four Bread; B sells up to four Bread and buys four Grain plus two Logs; C sells four Grain and buys two Flour before returning\. All orders use minimum one and Skip\. Purchases retain 100 company coins and cap each order at 200\. You must build the eligible Bakery and fund wages yourself; the example creates no stock, facilities or money\.

The live planner shows actual dock or voyage, next stop and action, cargo and an authoritative blocker\. Expand Cargo and committed route state for daily budget and last outcome; inspect an action for current source stock, market funds and quote\. Pass count advances when leaving the last listed stop, so an initial middle\-stop pass is not a completed circuit\. Inspect harbor returns to ordinary trading\. Back returns to the prior screen or overlay\.

Schema5 retains itinerary format1 plans, exact stop/action/cycle, last outcome and daily budget across mid\-stop and mid\-voyage saves\. Load continues the exact next work; Retry starts fresh with the same identity\.
